key_insight: Raising cold-spray pressure increases copper particle velocity enough to improve bonding, refine microstructure, and shift deposits toward a stronger, more ductile, and more conductive state.
engineering_relevance: For CSAM copper parts, spray pressure is a key process lever to balance electrical conductivity with mechanical integrity, making high-pressure operation the most promising window for functional components.
method: Cold-sprayed copper at 30, 40, 50, and 60 bar using a LightSPEE3D system.
Characterised deposits with XRD, SEM, hardness, eddy current conductivity, and tensile testing.
Linked particle velocity and microstructure to property changes across the pressure range.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that higher pressure increased particle velocity, crystallite refinement, conductivity, and ductility, while hardness decreased due to recovery/recrystallisation.
watch_item: The optimal high-pressure window may depend on system settings and substrate/deposition conditions, so the result should not be assumed to transfer directly to other CSAM platforms without validation.
paper_title: Optimising Cold Spray Additive Manufacturing: Pressure-driven enhancement of mechanical performance in copper deposits
